chapters.title: Cropping Patterns, Irrigation and Water-Use Efficiency
simple: **Wheat-paddy monoculture** hurts soil and water.
Fix with **diversification, millets/pulses, micro-irrigation**.
terms: One crop repeated on the same land.

body: Monoculture = only one crop on a piece of land. Punjab case: wheat and paddy cover 84.6% of cropped area, crowding out pulses, maize, bajra, oilseeds, cotton.

notes: Pests and disease rise with repeated crops (less genetic diversity)
Wheat and paddy do not fix nitrogen → soil nutrient depletion, more chemical fertiliser and pesticide
Aquifer depletion: CGWB 2024 Punjab — 153 blocks: 115 over-exploited, 4 critical, 12 semi-critical, 22 safe
Biodiversity loss; climate stress; paddy gives fewer man-days
Five factor groups: resource · technology · household · price · institutional/infrastructure
Small farms: food/fodder self-sufficiency, size, investment limits; large farms: relative prices; better irrigated areas more market-driven
Economic factors dominate with irrigation, infrastructure, rural markets, short-duration and drought-tolerant varieties

notes.ca: Economic Survey data: agri and allied ≈ 20% of national income, 46.1% of workforce. FY16-25 growth: fishing 8.8% > livestock 7.1% > crops 3.5%. Horticulture 362.08 MT > foodgrain 329.68 MT. Foodgrain 3,577.3 LMT (AY 2024-25, +254.3 LMT). India: largest dry-onion producer (~25%), 2nd in vegetables, fruits, potatoes. Yields below world in cereals, maize, soybean, pulses (groundnut exception).

notes: El Nino: 15 of 27 years hurt pulses; area -2 to -9%, output -6 to -30%; 2023-24 pulse imports +84% to 4.739 MT
La Nina: 13 of 25 years gained; 8 still lost (excess/ill-timed rain)
MP and Gujarat lead pulses (black soil rotations; short-duration varieties; high SRR) — NITI Aayog 2025
Water certainty, nutrient uptake, resilience, diversification, multiple cropping
PMKSY: coordinated farm-level investment, assured irrigation, on-farm efficiency, precision irrigation, aquifer recharge, private investment
Per Drop More Crop: 55% aid to small/marginal, 45% others
Disparity: <15% millets, ~26% pulses, ~67% rice
Priority: lagging states and crops; rejuvenate water bodies and surface storage (best returns); reuse treated wastewater peri-urban

body: PYQ hook (WUE 2016): water-use efficiency = crop per drop; micro-irrigation (drip, sprinkler) raises it by cutting evaporation and conveyance losses; link to PMKSY-PDMC and 2021 water crisis answer.

notes.ca: Beed (Maharashtra) experiment: Krishikul / Global Vikas Trust — farmers moved from soybean/cotton to fruit (papaya, custard apple, sweet lime, guava, pomegranate, mulberry, banana). TISS 2024: per-acre income ~₹38,700 → ~₹3.93 lakh (10X).

body: Crop Diversification Programme (RKVY) promotes alternate crops and legumes to restore fertility.

terms: Payout triggered by a weather index rather than farm-level loss.

notes.ca: MSP: 22 mandated crops; since Budget 2018-19 at least 50% over weighted average cost (A2+FL). Wheat MSP ₹2,585/qtl ≈ 109% above A2+FL. PM-KISAN: ₹4.09 lakh cr over 21 instalments; PM-Kisan Maandhan 24.92 lakh enrolled (Dec 2025).

notes: Cost data lag 2-3 years (input shocks, e.g. Hormuz 2026)
Wheat gets stronger support than other rabi crops
MSP works only where procurement works (wheat, paddy); weak for pulses, oilseeds, millets

notes: Farm-level loss missed (Palghar farmer ₹2.30) · trust deficit · voluntary enrolment → adverse selection · fiscal stress (Bihar, Jharkhand, WB opted out) · tenants excluded
Farmer-sensitive tech + local verification · timely settlement · link insurer pay to claim performance · parametric insurance · keep insurance as real risk cover
High buffer stock and carrying cost; public money locked; imports of edible oil (56%) and pulses persist; rice-wheat bias

Crop-shift incentives (per-acre/quintal) starting in eastern and central India · link with national priorities (maize, oilseeds for ethanol/feed) · Centre-State partnership · price-deficiency payments, bonuses, assured offtake · phased, flexible buffer norms

chapters.title: Genome-Edited Rice, Swaminathan and Seed Sovereignty
simple: Genome-edited ≠ GM (**no foreign DNA**).
terms: Site-Directed Nuclease type of genome editing.

notes.ca: Genome-edited rice (ICAR): DRR Dhan 100 Kamala (from Samba Mahsuri; CKX2 gene → more grains/panicle; ~20 days earlier; +19% yield; less water and methane) and Pusa DST Rice 1 (from MTU 1010; drought, salinity, alkalinity tolerance; +9.66-30.4% in saline/alkaline soils). Made with CRISPR-Cas SDN-1/SDN-2; no foreign DNA, so not GM (SDN-3 not used).

head: Significance
Concerns
rows: Biosafety: Coalition for a GM-Free India says edits not always precise; SDN-1/2 deregulation challenged
Labelling; loss of rice genetic diversity

notes: Transparent trials and post-release monitoring · crop-specific guidelines · affordable public seed · conserve indigenous varieties (e.g. Pokkali saline-tolerant paddy) · local training

Farmer-first science; institutions (CRRI, IARI, IRRI), MSSRF Chennai

Food → nutrition security · Evergreen Revolution (no cost to soil, water, biodiversity) · farmer income debate · mangroves and coastal protection · pro-poor, pro-women, pro-nature

chapters.title: Cotton: Productivity Crisis and Policy Dilemma
simple: Cotton problem = **productivity, technology, policy**.

notes.ca: 2nd-largest producer (after China); ~60 lakh farmers; value chain employs 4.5 crore. Production 13.6 m bales (2002-03) → 39.8 m (2013-14) with Bt cotton, then stagnated; yield ~441-448 kg/ha (20+ countries higher). Arrivals ~292 lakh bales vs need ~337 lakh. 11% import duty temporarily removed.

Flexible duty · CCI procurement on price fall · revive seed innovation with stable approvals · Cotton Productivity Mission · balance value chain · rainfed varieties

terms: Biofuel usable in existing engines without modification.

E85 launched at 48 outlets on World Environment Day 2026 (500 by Dec 2026; ~5,000 by Dec 2027); E100 rules drafted. BIS IS 19850:2026 for E22/E25/E27/E30. notes: 1G: food crops (sugar, wheat); fuel vs food → 2G: waste, residues, non-food biomass → 3G: engineered crops, algae → 4G: biomass + carbon capture → carbon negative
Economic: import substitution, rural value chains, farmer income, residue use

Environment: E20 cuts CO ~50% (2-wheelers), ~30% (4-wheelers); HC ~20%; circular economy
Strategic: energy security, oil-shock resilience, Global Biofuels Alliance, bridge to EV and hydrogen

Water: sugarcane + paddy ≈ 70% of irrigation; sugar price rise
NOx not uniformly lower; carbonyls; mileage loss; older vehicles; engine tuning and ethanol-resistant parts; storage/blending logistics; 2G scaling; chokepoints (Hormuz)

notes: Shift to 2G · lifecycle assessment · keep E10 protection-grade · uniform quality and labelling · recalibrate targets/feedstock incentives · use biofuels as strategic buffer

chapters.title: Disaster Management: Concepts, Institutions and DM Act 2005
chapters.pages: DM Static (class slides, handwritten) + DM PYQ sheet
simple: **Disaster = hazard + vulnerability − coping capacity**.
India: **reactive → proactive**; **DM Act 2005, NDMA, NDRF**.
terms: Ability to absorb, adapt and recover from a disaster.

body: Disaster = serious disruption of a community causing widespread human, material, economic or environmental loss that exceeds its own coping capacity. Hazard = potential source of harm (not certain). Vulnerability = conditions that raise susceptibility to harm. Exposure = assets in hazard-prone areas.
Disaster = Hazard × Vulnerability ÷ Capacity to cope · Risk = Hazard × Exposure × Vulnerability · Hazard groups: geophysical, hydrological, climatological, meteorological, biological.

notes: Physical (wooden houses)
Economic (low ability to cope)
Social (vulnerable sections)
Environmental (loss of wetlands)
Attitudinal (community attitudes)
UN: systematic use of administrative decisions, organisation and skills to lessen hazard impact — before, during, after
Goals: reduce losses, ensure prompt assistance, achieve rapid and effective recovery
Mitigation / prevention → Preparedness: prediction and early warning → DISASTER IMPACT → Response: impact assessment, relief → Recovery: reconstruct

body: DM Act 2005 covers: prevention; mitigation; capacity-building; preparedness; prompt response; severity assessment; evacuation, rescue, relief; rehabilitation and reconstruction.

notes: Pre-independence: relief, reactive → Post-1947: relief commissioners → 1990s: DM cell in Agriculture Ministry; IDNDR → 2000s: High Powered Committee after Odisha cyclone, Bhuj, etc. → DM Act 2005: proactive, multi-hazard
CCS → NCMC (national crisis management; command, control, coordination; CBRN emergencies)
NDMA — policies, plans, guidelines; chaired by PM
NEC — assists NDMA (Home Secretary leads)
NDRF — assists states; NIDM — training, capacity building
State: SDMA → DDMA → local bodies
Successes: Nepal earthquake 2015, Chennai floods 2015, Cyclone Fani 2019 — "golden hours", advanced preparedness
Challenge: CBRN emergencies
Financial devolution to State authorities weak
Centralisation
Definition of disaster not expanded (no objective severity threshold)
Response funds do not cover prevention, mitigation, risk reduction
"Visible goals" (relief) outrank "foundational goals" (prevention, training, awareness)
NDM Policy 2009 (framework for all phases) · NDMP 2019 (dynamic document, aligned to Sendai, aims at risk understanding, DRR investment, governance, Build Back Better)

notes.ca: National Project for Strengthening Community-Based DRR in PRIs (MoPR + NDMA): ₹507.37 cr; 20 States, 81 hazard-prone districts, 20 GPs per district in clusters; 20 Model GPs (₹5 cr per State = ₹100 cr) for flash floods, landslides, coastal erosion, cyclones, drought, earthquakes. Village DM plans integrated into GPDPs; builds on DMP-MoPR 2022.

body: Community participation answer: first responders; local knowledge; cyclone shelters and early warning dissemination; challenges — low awareness, resource gap, top-down plans, gender and equity gaps; measures — training, village plans in GPDP, SHGs, volunteers (Aapda Mitra), local-language alerts.

PYQ map: 2013 vulnerability/risk assessment · 2014 drought, El Niño/La Niña · 2015 earthquake · 2016 urban floods, cloudburst · 2017 tsunami · 2018, 2024 Sendai/DRR · 2019, 2021 landslides · 2020 proactive measures · 2022 cloudburst, coastal erosion · 2023 dam failure · 2024 urban floods · 2025 seawater intrusion · 2026 infrastructure vs DRR; community participation.

chapters.title: Global Frameworks and DRR Financing
simple: **Yokohama → Hyogo → Sendai** moved from relief to **risk reduction**.
India funds through **SDRMF/NDRMF 80:20**.
notes: 1972 UN disaster relief office → 1990 IDNDR → 1994 Yokohama Strategy → 2005 Hyogo Framework (Kobe) → 2015 Sendai Framework (2015-30)
Hyogo successes: reduced mortality, cost-effectiveness of DRR, a global platform, first plan from all sectors
Challenges: disasters still take a heavy toll; economic losses; need for a more comprehensive framework → Sendai
Sendai shift: from managing disasters to managing risk (general knowledge: 4 priorities, 7 targets — verify)

body: Three post-2015 frameworks are coherent: Sendai · Paris Agreement · SDGs. India's 10-Point Agenda: mainstream DRR in development; risk coverage for all; women's leadership; global risk mapping; technology; university network; social media and mobiles; local capacity; learn after every disaster; coherent international response.

notes: CDRI (India-led, now ~40 countries) · Suva Expert Dialogue on Loss and Damage · Loss and Damage Fund · Global Platform for DRR reviews Sendai · EW4All (WMO + UNDRR, universal early warning by end-2027) · ARISE India (CII, FICCI) · Nature-based solutions (Mula-Mutha Pune)

notes.ca: 15th FC: created SDRMF and NDRMF; split 80% response funds (SDRF/NDRF) and 20% mitigation funds. Within 80%: 40% response and relief · 30% recovery and reconstruction (₹20,539 cr NDRF; ₹48,046 cr SDRF; needs PDNA) · 10% preparedness. SDRF contribution 75:25, 90:10 for NE and Himalayan States.

notes: Outdated relief norms (₹4 lakh for life; ₹1.2 lakh full house loss)
Rigid spending (relief only)
No objective classification of severe disaster
Procedural delays: State memorandum → IMCT → HLC
Update norms · Disaster Risk / Vulnerability Index triggers · drone surveys, digital assessment, PFMS tracking · PPPs, targeted funds, tax incentives

notes.ca: UNDRR GAR 2025 "Resilience Pays": DRR is investment; disaster costs > $2.3 trn/yr including cascading; direct costs rose from ~$70-80 bn/yr (1970-2000) to ~$180-200 bn/yr (2001-20).

chapters.title: Space Technology and Cell Broadcast Alerts in DM
simple: **Space** gives data, **CBS** gives last-mile alerts.
terms: Common Alerting Protocol recommended by ITU.

head: Component
Use and example
rows: Hazard zonation; NRSC Landslide Atlas 2023; Flood Hazard Atlas (Assam, Bihar)
Cyclone Dana 2024 tracking; forest fire alerts (FSI, MODIS/VIIRS)
Satellite links; National Cyclone Risk Mitigation Project dissemination

NISAR maps land and ice every 12 days

body: Conclusion line: space technology moves DM from relief-centric to risk-informed, anticipatory governance; integrate with community action.
CBS — DoT + NDMA; indigenous, built by C-DOT. Sends alerts to all mobile devices in a defined area at once, without straining networks (unlike SMS). Upgrades SACHET (CAP standard, SMS, also C-DOT).

notes: Near real-time · works on almost all handsets · no personal data · no app or subscription · multilingual · distinct tone even on silent · message stays until acknowledged

simple: National security covers **13 elements**, not only the army.
Economic, energy, cyber, health, food, water and disaster security are part of it.
terms: Freedom to take defence and foreign-policy decisions without dependence on another power.
Using trade, sanctions or supply cut-offs to pressure a country.

notes.h: The big picture (my grouping to remember 13 elements)

What it means
Detail to quote

chapters.title: National Security Doctrine
simple: India has a security strategy in practice but no public **National Security Strategy**.
The case for one: new domains, proxy wars, blurred internal-external threats, and theaterisation.
terms: Hostile actions short of open war, e.g. cyber, proxies, disinformation.
Merging army, navy, air force into joint regional commands.

body: National Security Doctrine = a set of basic principles, based on the core interests of the State, shaping how different elements of national power protect and further the Republic's interests; a concise summary of strategic vision and objectives. It identifies missions and principles for the armed forces, diplomatic and intelligence communities.
"The new frontiers of war — fourth-generation warfare — is civil society." — Ajit Doval
"Half-done reforms create new vulnerabilities without solving old ones. You cannot cross a chasm in two leaps." — Shivshankar Menon (Bipin Rawat's reforms incomplete)

notes.ca: In the news: India still debates a public, comprehensive National Security Strategy; meanwhile elements are codified through domain-specific doctrines (counter-terrorism, cyberspace, multi-domain operations).

notes: Complex threats — traditional + non-traditional (cyber, narco-terror, eco-terror)
Technology expands the battlefield and nullifies traditional advantage
Grey-zone warfare — ambiguous space between peace and war
Digital age reshapes battlespace; proxy wars rise
